title: A Survey of OCR Evaluation Methods and Metrics and the Invisibility of Historical Documents

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic review of OCR evaluation benchmarks (using the PRISMA framework) to identify the exclusion of marginalized community-produced archives, followed by a qualitative case study testing state-of-the-art OCR models on the complex layouts of historical Black newspapers.

Analyzing representational harm and algorithmic invisibility by assessing how standard OCR systems fail to accurately digitize the early Black press (e.g., The Weekly Advocate), thereby erasing editorial logic and rendering Black historical narratives computationally inaccessible.

Comparing the training data composition and evaluation metrics of modern OCR systems on contemporary documents (e.g., born-digital PDFs, modern corporate forms) versus degraded historical scans featuring archaic typography (e.g., 19th-century Gothic typefaces) and microfilm artifacts.
